Definition: from G4253 and G1097; to know beforehand, i.e. foresee:--foreknow (ordain), know (before).
BiblicalUsage: Proginosko means to know beforehand, to foreknow, and Paul builds the doctrine of election on it. Whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son. Peter says Christ was foreordained before the foundation of the world, and the Jews knew Paul from the beginning, while Peter warns believers who know these things before to beware.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe foreknowledge is God's knowing love, not cold foresight: he knew his people before he called them, and his knowing is what makes them his. That is why nothing can separate us from the love that knew us first.
